3. Plaintiffs claimed that Amir Kha, the predecessor-in-interest of both the plaintiffs and the defendants was the original owner of the schedule land who died leaving behind 3 sons Haban Ali, Mofiz Ali and Nochin who got 1/3 share each of the properties left by Amir Kha. Thereby the plaintiffs as successive successors of the original owner Amir Kha inherited .50 decimals of land out of 3 acres .57 decimals of land as shown in the schedule to the plaint. The aforesaid suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-4. Defendant Nos. 1-12 and 14 appeared in the suit and filed written statement but, ultimately, did not contest the suit. The plaintiff and the defendant Nos. 1-4 adduced evidence in support of their respective claims and the learned Assistant Judge, Balaganj, on consideration of the facts circumstances and evidence adduced by the parties, dismissed the suit against which the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being No. 218 of 2002 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet. The plaintiff-appellants in that appeal prayed for dispensing with the service of notices upon the respondent Nos. 4-62, as they did not contest the suit, whereupon the learned District Judge allowed the prayer on the same date. Thereafter the defendant Nos. 1-4 as respondent Nos. 1-4 together with the plaintiff-appellants filed a petition for compromise of the suit amongst themselves on 13.3.2000 which was allowed on 31.8.2003 upon examining two witnesses. Accordingly, the appeal was allowed on compromise in terms of the solenama which did form part of the decree. 

 6. Mr. Md. Faroque Ahmed, assisted by Ms. Anjuman Ara Begum, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the defendant Nos. 8-12 and 14(present opposite party Nos. 1-6) appeared in the Title Suit No. 50 of 2001 and filed written statement but ultimately did not contest the suit. Subsequently, the plaintiffs preferred appeal being No. 218 of 2002 against the judgment and decree passed in the aforesaid suit dismissing the same wherein the plaintiff-appellants prayed for dispensing with the service of summons and notices upon the respondents (including the non-contesting defendant Nos. 8-12 and 14) and the petition was allowed and, ultimately, the appeal was allowed on compromise in terms of the solenama 'filed by the plaintiff-appellants and respondent Nos. 1-4 (defendant Nos.1-4). The learned Advocate further submits that since the learned District Judge, Sylhet on prayer of the appellants allowed dispensing with the service of summons and notices upon the defendants 8-12 and 14 as being non-contesting defendants, the Court, thereafter should not have allowed the said defendant-respondents an opportunity to rehear the appeal and as such the impugned judgment and order allowing rehearing of the appeal is not sustainable in law. Moreso, the said Miscellaneous application was time barred and not in form and as such the same is also not sustainable in law.
